standard.title: Read and write high-frequency words
standard.description: read and write some high-frequency words and other familiar words
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can decode CVC words phonically (AC9EFLY12). They have not yet been asked to build a set of words that are recognised and written automatically — including high-frequency words that cannot always be decoded phonically.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can read and write an increasing number of high-frequency words and other familiar words — including words that cannot be fully decoded phonically — with sufficient automaticity to support fluent reading and independent writing.

nodes.label: Some words are recognised at sight
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise at least ten high-frequency words automatically — without needing to decode them phoneme by phoneme.
nodes.minimum_width: Read at least ten high-frequency words on sight without decoding.
nodes.typical_width: Read an increasing number of high-frequency words recognised in shared and independent texts; recognise some familiar words (own name, character names, school name).
wider: Read high-frequency words in connected text — applying recognition in the context of reading rather than word list drills only
Compare which words appear most often across multiple familiar texts — building a text-grounded high-frequency word list
Investigate high-frequency words in digital texts — noting which appear on screens, websites, apps and digital books
nodes.hinge_reason: Sight recognition of high-frequency words is a prerequisite for fluent written production in Node 2 — students who cannot recognise these words automatically in reading also cannot write them automatically, and their writing composition is impeded by the need to decode or invent every common word.

response_modes.reason: High-frequency word recognition must become automatic — slow recognition of common words significantly limits reading fluency. Repeated exposure across many encounters is the mechanism. Width is thin here: the issue is automaticity, not contextual breadth.

success_criteria: Student reads at least ten high-frequency words automatically without sounding out.
Student recognises their own name and at least five other familiar words on sight.

nodes.label: High-frequency words can be written
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can write at least some high-frequency words correctly from memory.
nodes.minimum_width: Write at least five high-frequency words correctly without copying.
nodes.typical_width: Read and write an increasing number of high-frequency words; write familiar words from memory in the context of independent writing tasks.
wider: Use high-frequency words in independent writing and self-check for correct spelling
Build a personal word card collection — connecting reading recognition with written production
Apply known high-frequency words as anchors in independent writing — using them alongside phonemic spelling strategies for unknown words

response_modes.reason: Written production of high-frequency words must be automatic — looking up or sounding out every common word in writing impedes composition. Practice to accuracy across multiple words is required.

success_criteria: Student can write at least five high-frequency words correctly from memory.
Student uses high-frequency words in independent writing without needing to copy them.
